lifecycle_acceptance_test_2026_09_23.prerequisite_fix: A plain POST /agents/deploy with no llm_provider_id failed with worker error code PROVIDER_STATE_REMOVED_DURING_DEPLOYMENT ('LLM provider state was removed while the runtime was provisioning') after 5 retries -> DLQ. Root cause: reconcileRuntimeLlmAuth (workers/provisioner/worker.ts) requires either LLM env vars or a defaultProvider once the container starts; a fresh user has neither unless a provider row exists. The built-in demo flow (POST /agents/activate-demo) creates one via llmProviders.ensureDemoProvider(userId), but that route hardcodes runtime_family='openclaw' and is also disabled in this fixture's platform config (capabilities.localDockerDemo.enabled=false), so it could not be used directly for a 'hermes' family agent. Fix: called llmProviders.ensureDemoProvider(userId) directly in-process (via `npx tsx` one-liner inside the running backend-api container, same DB pool/env), which is runtime-family-agnostic and just inserts/updates a normal 'demo' provider row (is_default=true for a provider-less user). This is worth carrying into N4 (provider-lock/lifecycle reliability) as a known gap: the generic deploy path has no equivalent safety net to the activate-demo advisory-lock + ensureDemoProvider pattern.
steps_and_evidence: Deploy A (runtime_family=hermes, backend_type=docker): queued -> deploying -> running in 64s.
Deploy B (same user, sequential after A reached running): queued -> deploying -> running in 64s. Distinct nora_hermes_home_<id> volume per agent.
Planted a unique marker file on A's persistent volume (/opt/data/n0-marker.txt) and a distinct marker on B's (/opt/data/b-marker.txt).
POST /agents/A/stop: API returned status=stopped; docker ps -a showed A Exited(0); B status/container_id/marker all unchanged (verified via API + docker inspect + docker exec cat).

POST /agents/A/start: A reached status=running in 8s (no re-pull/re-bootstrap needed); A's marker file was still present (same volume reused, data survived restart); B's container_id and marker were unchanged throughout.

DELETE /agents/A: API returned success; A's container fully removed from docker ps -a; GET /agents/A returned HTTP 404; A's nora_hermes_home volume was also removed (full teardown on explicit delete, unlike the 'keep volumes on retry/replacement' behavior seen during the earlier failed-deploy retries); B's status, exact container_id, and marker file were all unchanged.
Cleanup: deleted agent B via the same API. Outer host resource check post-test: Mem 3.1Gi/7.7Gi used (4.6Gi available), Swap 2.5Gi/4Gi, disk 61G/123G (50%) -- stable, no leak observed from this test.
